notes: RECALL TIE (reproduced): 23/23 assertions both arms, matching iteration-2 exactly (same hard/subtle set, re-run fresh on Sonnet). Every subtle planted vuln — JWT kid path-traversal/key-swap, OAuth state-CSRF, TOCTOU/idempotency races, bcrypt 72-byte truncation, non-constant-time secure_compare, bypassable SSRF blocklist, path-containment prefix bug, blacklist stored-XSS — caught by BOTH arms in BOTH independent runs.

PRECISION EDGE REPRODUCES (on a DIFFERENT file each time): with_skill is 0 FP across both hard-set runs (iteration-2: 0/29; iteration-4: 0/31 -- flawless in every single hard-set review across this whole investigation, 60/60 findings clean). without_skill makes exactly ONE false positive per 5-file hard-set run in BOTH iterations (iteration-2: kid/JWT file; iteration-4: crypto_utils file -- a different file each time, so it isn't the same specific miss repeating, but the RATE (~1 FP per hard 5-file set) is now a twice-observed pattern, not a single-run fluke.

THOROUGHNESS FAVORS BASELINE (reproduced in DIRECTION, not magnitude): without_skill found more total legitimate issues in BOTH hard-set runs (iteration-2: 33 vs 29 TP; iteration-4: 34 vs 31 TP -- baseline +3-4 both times). Combined with the precision result above, the emerging shape on SUBTLE vulnerabilities specifically is: baseline is slightly more exploratory/thorough but takes on a small, consistent false-positive rate; the skill's structured walk-through is perfectly clean but marginally narrower.

OUTPUT-QUALITY NOTE (not captured by the TP/FP ledger): the eval-2 (fetcher/SSRF) grader independently verified with_skill's Finding 1 overstated which IP encodings bypass the blocklist (claimed 2130706433/0x7f000001/0177.0.0.1 as bypasses; Node's URL parser actually canonicalizes and blocks all three) -- without_skill got this technical nuance right. This didn't flip the finding to a false positive (the overall SSRF claim is still valid, just one supporting example was wrong) but IS exactly the kind of output-consistency defect that binary TP/FP scoring can't see, and this instance favors the baseline -- a caution against reading the precision-ledger tie/edge as the whole quality picture.

COST: with_skill 1.31x tokens (103.6k vs 79.0k) -- close to iteration-2's 1.29x, confirming the ~1.3x hard-set token premium is stable across runs. Wall-clock is now essentially at parity (1.01x) -- on Sonnet, the skill's time overhead has fully washed out; only the token premium remains.

CROSS-ITERATION SYNTHESIS (4 iterations, 2 model tiers x 2 difficulty levels, 40 total reviews): recall NEVER differed -- 100%/100% in all four. The skill's only reproducible signal is a precision/thoroughness TRADE-OFF that appears specifically on SUBTLE vulnerabilities and only on Sonnet-tier execution: the skill trades a few points of raw thoroughness for a flawless false-positive record, at a stable ~1.3x token cost. This is more informative than 'no difference' but still does not, by itself, justify a rewrite -- it argues for preserving the Exploitability Discipline section (the apparent source of the precision edge) rather than trimming pattern lists, and for treating weak-model (Haiku) performance as the remaining open question.
